chunks: From him, from Ya'qub, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Fadhl, from Shu'ayb al-Aqarqufi, from Abu Hamzah al-Thumali, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: "The earth will not remain empty of a scholar from us who knows the truth from the falsehood."

He said: "Taqiyyah (dissimulation/prudence) was instituted only to preserve blood [from being shed]. So when Taqiyyah itself leads to bloodshed, then (it is no longer valid). By God's oath, if you were called to support us, you would say, 'We will not do it; we only practice Taqiyyah,' and Taqiyyah would be more beloved to you than your fathers and mothers.
And if the Qa'im (peace be upon him) arose, he would not need to question you about that, and he would establish God's punishment upon many of you who are of the people of hypocrisy."

key_terms.التَّقِيَّة: Taqiyyah (prudent dissimulation or concealment of faith)

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for the validity of Taqiyyah according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes the continuity of divine guidance through an infallible scholar from the Ahl al-Bayt who distinguishes truth from falsehood, ensuring the preservation of the faith. He clarifies that Taqiyyah is a strategic tool for survival rather than an end in itself, warning that when it becomes a habitual excuse for avoiding duty, it signifies spiritual decay. The Imam further notes that the eventual rise of the Qa'im will expose the hypocrisy of those who used Taqiyyah as a cover for cowardice, leading to their accountability.
